extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, auditors/attestation providers, and securities lawyers advising on SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Final SEC rules (Items 1505/1506) specifying mandatory third‑party attestation/assurance requirements for registrants' Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions disclosures, including scope, phase‑in timelines, acceptable assurance levels, filing/timing rules, exemptions, and voluntary assurance treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory attestation for Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions (Item 1506)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the final rules (Item 1506(a)(1)) a registrant, including a foreign private issuer, that is required to provide Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions disclosure pursuant to Item 1505 must include an attestation report covering the disclosure of its Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions in the relevant filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attestation engagement must, at a minimum, meet the assurance level and compliance dates specified by filer type. The Commission adopted final rules requiring attestation to provide investors with an additional degree of reliability regarding figures, key assumptions, methodologies, and data sources used to arrive at GHG figures (see pp. 21744–21746). Modifications were made from the proposal to address commenter concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered filers and scope (AFs and LAFs; exclusion of SRCs and EGCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules apply the attestation requirements to Accelerated Filers (AFs) and Large Accelerated Filers (LAFs). The final rules exempt Smaller Reporting Companies (SRCs) and Emerging Growth Companies (EGCs) from the requirement to obtain an attestation report because those entities are exempted from the requirement to disclose GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application is consistent with Item 1505's scope; the rules also state they will not apply to a private company that is a party to certain business combination transactions (Securities Act Rule 165(f)). The decision to exempt SRCs and EGCs was driven by the decision to exempt these companies from the disclosure requirement (pp. 21744–21747).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance levels and phased compliance schedule (limited then reasonable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules require limited assurance for AFs and LAFs beginning the third fiscal year after the Item 1505 compliance date; LAFs must obtain reasonable assurance beginning the seventh fiscal year after the Item 1505 compliance date. AFs are not required to scale up to reasonable assurance under the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule includes a concrete schedule (illustrative table): LAFs — disclosure compliance FY2026, limited assurance FY2029, reasonable assurance FY2033; AFs (other than SRCs and EGCs) — disclosure compliance FY2028, limited assurance FY2031, reasonable assurance N/A. The phased approach is intended to give registrants and assurance providers time to prepare and to limit burdens on smaller/smaller sophisticated issuers (pp. 21744–21747, 21748–21749).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of limited assurance vs reasonable assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission did not define 'limited assurance' and 'reasonable assurance' in the final rules because these are defined by prevailing attestation standards; however, the rules describe the typical differences in procedures and outcomes between the two levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical procedural differences: limited assurance engagements generally involve analytical procedures and inquiries; reasonable assurance engagements also require risk assessment and detail testing procedures. Outcome differences: reasonable assurance yields positive assurance (an opinion that disclosures are in accordance with Item 1505 in all material respects); limited assurance yields negative assurance (a conclusion about whether the provider is aware of material modifications needed). The Commission expects the assurance report to describe the work performed to facilitate investor understanding (pp. 21738–21740, 21746–21749).

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandatory assurance over Scope 3 emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require any registrants to obtain assurance over Scope 3 emissions; Item 1506 does not impose assurance obligations for Scope 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although commenters recommended requiring assurance over Scope 3 (with varying views on level of assurance), the Commission narrowed the final rules such that no registrants will be required to obtain assurance over Scope 3 emissions (pp. 21742–21744).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary assurance: disclosure and applicable requirements (Item 1506(e) and Items 1506(b)–(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of voluntary assurance depends on timing and whether the registrant is subject to Items 1505/1506: (a) For registrants subject to Items 1505 and 1506, any voluntary assurance over GHG emissions before the assurance compliance date must comply with Item 1506(e). (b) After the assurance compliance date, voluntary assurance over GHG emissions not required to be assured must follow Items 1506(b)–(d), including using the same attestation standard as the required assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants not subject to Items 1505 or 1506 that voluntarily obtain assurance must comply with Item 1506(e). The Commission narrowed the scope of voluntary-assurance-related rules to apply primarily to GHG emissions disclosures (pp. 21748–21749). The rules aim to promote comparability and consistency by prescribing minimum requirements for voluntary assurance that relates to assured items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional election to obtain higher level of assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: During the phased-in compliance period registrants that are subject to assurance requirements may elect to obtain a higher level of assurance than required (e.g., an LAF may elect reasonable assurance while limited assurance is required; an AF may elect reasonable assurance at its option).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules expressly permit registrants to obtain any level of assurance over GHG emissions disclosures not required to be assured under Item 1506(a), but after the assurance compliance date, voluntary assurance must follow Items 1506(b)–(d) if relevant (pp. 21748–21749, 21756–21763).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing timing, incorporation by reference, and attestation report deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: GHG emissions metrics required by Item 1505 in an annual Form 10‑K may be incorporated by reference from the registrant's Form 10‑Q for the second fiscal quarter of the fiscal year immediately following the year to which the GHG disclosure relates, or included in an amended annual report on Form 10‑K no later than the due date for such Form 10‑Q. The deadline extension for GHG emissions metrics also applies to the deadline for the filing of the attestation report accompanying the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This additional time (an additional two fiscal quarters) is intended to provide registrants and attestation providers sufficient time to measure emissions, provide assurance, and prepare the required attestation report. Registrants that elect to incorporate by reference or to amend must include an express statement in the annual report indicating that intention (pp. 21744–21745, 21748–21749).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of attestation report within filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require the attestation report to be included in a separately captioned 'Climate‑Related Disclosure' section; placement of climate-related disclosures (other than financial statement disclosures) is largely left to each registrant's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the proposal would have required a separate caption, the final rules leave placement to registrants, who may nevertheless elect to include a separately captioned section (pp. 21748–21749). The Commission retained requirements about the content and standards of the attestation report regardless of placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation standard and expectation that report describe work performed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission expects assurance engagements to be performed in accordance with prevailing attestation standards that meet requirements detailed in the rules; the Commission declined to define 'limited' and 'reasonable' assurance itself and instead relies on standard‑setters' definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission expects the description of the work performed to be included in any assurance report issued under the final rules, which should facilitate investor understanding of the nature of the limited or reasonable assurance engagement. Some commenters recommended defining terms if the Commission allowed standards other than AICPA, IAASB, or PCAOB (pp. 21738–21740, 21746–21749).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of separate management assessment or attestation of controls over GHG disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposing Release asked whether the Commission should require a registrant to provide a separate management assessment and disclosure of the effectiveness of controls over GHG emissions disclosure, or require an attestation report covering the effectiveness of such GHG emissions controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters were split: some supported a separate management assessment to strengthen validity of data; others said existing DCP requirements suffice and the incremental benefit may not justify the cost. Some commenters opposed requiring attestation on controls due to lack of a specific standard for non‑financial data controls and subject matter expertise concerns. The final rules' treatment of this point is discussed in greater detail elsewhere in the release; the Commission considered but did not finalize a commission‑defined separate controls definition in this section (pp. 21740–21744).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for certain private companies in business combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules, including Item 1506, will not apply to a private company that is a party to a business combination transaction, as defined by Securities Act Rule 165(f), involving a securities offering registered on Form S‑4 or F‑4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This carve‑out limits application of the attestation requirement in the specific context of private companies that are parties to such registered business combination transactions (p. 21744).
